ruleChanges.before: AND across predicates, OR across each predicate's literal terms. Include ordinary synonyms needed for the requested concept; never copy the user's sentence.
ruleChanges.after: AND across predicates, OR across each predicate's literal terms. For match_record_body_text, include only USER-requested content conditions and ordinary synonyms; never copy the user's sentence or use record-type/source labels as body terms unless their literal content is requested.

ruleChanges.before: Minimal search concept for the event, without pet name or temporal instructions. Every normalized term must occur in the record; terms need not be adjacent. Code resolves the actual dated event. Never guess its date.
ruleChanges.after: Literal identifying concept for the referenced saved event. Preserve explicit identifying qualifiers from the USER reference, including a year or quoted title; do not discard them as temporal instructions. Every normalized term must occur in stored title/note; terms need not be adjacent. Code resolves the actual event and date. Never guess an anchor date or resolve multiple matching events by preference.

ruleChanges.before: Requested proposition: stored_report only for exact stored wording, attributed reports or a timeline of statements; it never establishes current/corrected truth or supersession. effective_fact for current, settled, corrected, definitive latest values and every historical calculation. Do not downgrade an effective-fact request because history might conflict. ruleChanges.after: Requested proposition: stored_report only for exact stored wording, attributed reports or a timeline of statements; it never establishes current/corrected truth or supersession. effective_fact for current, settled, corrected, definitive latest values and every historical calculation. sourceMetadataDifferences.currentSource: Every pure saved-history read MUST emit readTicket. Use read for record selection; read_since_event only when temporal.anchor names an event. Anchor relation is from (inclusive), after (exclusive), or before (exclusive). Never guess event dates or an undated request's cutoff. Use predicates only for USER-requested restrictions on the bodies of stored records, with literal text_any terms and ordinary synonyms. Record types, source labels and date/subject locators do not by themselves restrict body contents. Only the typed ticket selects time and records: temporal constrains the window; selection carries grouped semantic ordering/cardinality; outputs.completeness describes the requested evidence obligation; outputs.ordering and outputs.limit control only presentation and transport for compositional reads. Classify completeness by the requested proposition: does answering require establishing the entire matching set in the requested domain, or only certifying selected results? For compositional ordered take, per-subject selection and unions of selected boundaries, use sufficient unless the user also requests an exhaustive proposition. An earliest or latest endpoint, top N, or two independent boundaries require endpoint/selection certification, not an exhaustive historical listing. Use exhaustive for complete matching sets, historical existence or absence, and exact counts over the requested domain. Temporal dates and resolved anchors restrict that domain; they do not by themselves decide completeness. This distinction is independent of topic, subject count, wording, presentation format and operation. Never infer exhaustive merely because history is long or the request spans all subjects. Setting sufficient does not establish certainty: organs must still certify every requested selection, and unresolved lineage, anchors or coverage remain limitations. These are semantic obligations, not keyword rules. Finite ordered takes are compositional selection obligations, including single-subject earliest/latest and top-N requests. Emit selection with the requested asc/desc order and take count, outputs.strategy omitted by the compositional branch, outputs.completeness sufficient unless the user separately asks for an exhaustive proposition, and temporal.calendar null unless the calendar itself is the requested semantic partition. Legacy chronological provider output is reserved for unbounded ordered retrieval and cannot carry a finite limit. Do not use oldest_year for the earliest measurement: the earliest matching measurement can be later than the oldest year of notes. Reserve oldest_year for an explicit request for the oldest calendar year of notes (including a topic filter within that explicitly requested year). Predicates match normalized token sequences with conservative regular inflection equivalence, never arbitrary substrings. Supply discriminating topic terms and ordinary synonyms. Search hints cannot supply predicate authority. A request for a recorded value and its date is a source-record lookup: quantity records; preserve its dated quotation. Deterministic arithmetic uses CalculatePlan with a read or read_since_event ticket; non-arithmetic comparisons may use compare or rank. Never invent a source value. Use mode read, evidenceBasis saved_history, no task/writeJob/frame. Ordinary record reads set readTicket.episode null. Genuine episode count or membership requests put the operation and referent in readTicket.episode; a missing referent stays missing and requires clarification. Count targets use scoped_register and no ordinal; membership targets use a displayed list or a scoped register with explicit ticket dates. Topic null preserves an unspecified count request for clarification. Episode counts require independently verified membership, never a count of returned notes. Legacy episodeTopic/ordinal cannot create this obligation. The server binds owned pet IDs. Requests with no saved-history job keep readTicket null; a mixed append plus history job supplies both appendJob and readTicket. Legacy from/to/terms/selection fields cannot override a readTicket. Choose one retrieval operation per readTicket. For any single retrieval, including operation read, read_since_event, compare, or an episode request carried by readTicket.episode, emit readTicket.probes: []. A value and its date, an earliest/latest record, a topic filter, and synonyms for that topic are parts of one retrieval, not distinct probes. Whenever predicates are nonempty, outputs.strategy is non-null, or outputs.limit is non-null, probes must be empty or null. Keep probes empty or null for read_since_event, compare and episode requests. For ordinary read, read_since_event and compare, encode requested factual topic semantics in predicates. Optional searchHints may duplicate those terms or suggest explanatory context, but never carry the only representation of requested meaning: hints cannot determine factual membership, ordering, completeness, or obligation support. Episode topics stay in episode.referent; preserve the episode contract's empty predicates and searchHints. Use ID-free readTicket.probes only for genuinely distinct independently requested probes. Each probe carries quote, sourceTurnId, petNames, from/to, target, termGroups and ordering. The server validates exact USER spans and authorized subjects, then assigns internal need IDs; never emit needId, id or sourceSpanId. For ticketed reads emit evidenceNeeds []: probes is the sole source of multi-need grounding, not a parallel evidenceNeeds list. Homogeneous work with the same predicate, temporal window/relation, ordering and cardinality across subjects uses compositional grouping/selection, not a probe per subject. Synonyms do not create separate obligations. In that multi-probe form, predicates must be [], searchHints empty or null, outputs.strategy null, and outputs.limit null; do not combine probe retrieval with a single-ticket filter, strategy or limit. Ground each need in exact user quotes and pet names, with its explicit window, optional ISO target day/month, ordered advisory termGroups, and asc/desc query ordering. Synonym termGroups alone do not justify needs. Preserve every distinct need before routine context.

Decompose grouped reads into the existing readTicket.selection, never a new operation or a sentence-specific intent. GROUPING: use groupBy [subject] when results must be independently selected for each resolved subject. Grouping never grants account scope; preserve named, selected, household and USER-established conversation subject authority. ORDERING: orderBy event_at asc or desc expresses semantic event order inside each group; outputs.ordering alone expresses presentation, not selection. TAKE: count with per group defines semantic cardinality; outputs.limit is a separate global transport limit and normally stays null for a compositional plan. UNION: use independent ordered clauses for multiple requested boundaries. PREDICATES: preserve requested body-content conditions regardless of grouping, using text_any with literal terms and ordinary synonyms; changing the topic or pets must not require a different operation. TEMPORAL: explicit from/to constraints compose with selection; never manufacture dates from an event name. A semantic temporal.anchor MAY compose with predicates and selection in a read_since_event ticket. Brain supplies the anchor concept and relation, never the ledger event or invented from/to dates. The deterministic temporal resolver resolves the USER-qualified concept against owned history under the explicit requested authority and establishes the concrete boundary before selection. For recorded statements relative to a recorded event, stored_report retains report-only authority and closed source/correction proof; effective_fact still requires certified effective truth. Preserve explicit identifying qualifiers such as a year or quoted event title in the anchor concept. Unmatched or ambiguous references remain limitations. Missing, ambiguous or uncertifiable anchors retain existing anchor limitations; never drop the anchor or fall back to whole history. Calendar selectors remain incompatible with selection. Ordinary anchored history retains its existing read_since_event ticket. SINGLE SUBJECT: do not introduce grouping when the existing ungrouped read expresses the request. MULTI-NEED: genuinely distinct requests use ID-free source-quoted probes, not a forced grouped selection. VALIDITY: choose exactly one semantic selection representation. With non-null selection, emit probes [], episode null and omit outputs.strategy entirely; no legacy semantic strategy may accompany selection. Semantic order and cardinality belong only in selection.orderBy and selection.take; outputs.ordering is presentation only and outputs.limit is a global transport cap, normally null, never a per-group count. With selection null, legacy outputs.strategy/order/limit retain their existing meaning. Use selection null when absent. AMBIGUITY: unresolved subjects or references require clarification under the existing subject/reference contract; do not guess additional subjects, an anchor, a grouping target or the requested fact. The server binder remains authoritative. Legacy envelope selection/from/to/terms do not provide a second plan or override readTicket.
